p.name: Poole
p.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
p.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house.
p.bio: Poole is the elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, obeyed by the housemaid, cook, and knife-boy, and directed by Mr. Utterson in the search. He is afraid and cannot bear it, with a white face and harsh broken voice. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, that Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, and that all servants had orders to obey Hyde. Later he reported Jekyll confined and silent, came to Utterson at night, and said he thought there had been foul play. He and Utterson broke in and found Hyde's body. He currently awaits Lanyon's arrival with a locksmith.

p.name: Dr. Jekyll
p.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
p.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
p.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

p.name: the man in the middle
p.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
p.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
p.bio: The man in the middle, later named Hyde, is a person of extraordinary appearance who gives a feeling of deformity. He is cool, sneering, and Satan-like. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, then was collared by Enfield and brought back to the group around the child. The doctor turned sick and white with desire to kill him. Threatened with scandal, he was forced to pay a hundred pounds. He led them to the door, unlocked it, and returned with gold and a cheque, offering to stay until the banks opened and cash it himself. They spent the night in Enfield's chambers and went to the bank next day. He still has a key and used it a week ago.

p.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. p.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
p.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
p.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

p.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

p.name: Mr. Utterson
p.intro: lawyer, friend of Enfield
p.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
p.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

p.name: Mr. Utterson
p.intro: lawyer, friend of Enfield
p.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
p.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

p.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
p.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
p.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

p.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

p.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, owner of the house with laboratory and cabinet, and the friend and client of Mr. Utterson. He is tall and well built, known for charities and religion, but has become fanciful and estranged from Dr. Lanyon. His will left all his possessions to Edward Hyde, and he admitted Hyde dictated its terms. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, then resumed his old friendships before shutting his door against Utterson and vowing extreme seclusion. He was last seen sitting sadly at the middle window, declining to walk out. He is said to have been made away with eight days ago, and his body has not been found.

p.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
p.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
p.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

p.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

p.name: Dr. Jekyll
p.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
p.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
p.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

p.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

p.intro: murder victim, an aged gentleman
p.tagline: Murder victim, an aged gentleman
p.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

p.name: Poole
p.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
p.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house
p.bio: Poole is the elderly butler of Dr. Jekyll's house and the servant who directs the search after the cabinet is broken open. He is frightened and worn, with a white face and a harsh broken voice, and for about a week he has been unable to bear the situation. He long served Jekyll, admitted Utterson to the cabinet, and reported that Jekyll confined himself over the laboratory. When he came to Utterson's house at night, he said the doctor had shut himself in and he feared foul play. He led Utterson to the laboratory, told of the masked figure, and struck the door with an axe. He now hands Utterson the sealed packet and awaits the police.

p.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
p.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
p.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
p.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

p.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
p.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
p.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。
